articles.headlineTranslated: Yokohama City University Identifies Nectin-4 as the Major Entry Receptor for Rubella Virus.
articles.summary: Rubella virus uses Nectin-4 as the major host cell entry receptor, a finding by a Yokohama City University–led team published in Nature (November 2026). Using rubella virus–like particles and CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screens, they show Nectin-4 mediates entry in airway epithelial cells and placental syncytiotrophoblasts. In air–liquid interface airway models, rubella infects from the basal surface and releases progeny apically; infection is markedly reduced by Nectin-4 inhibition. Placental organoids reveal high Nectin-4 on syncytiotrophoblast surfaces, with infection suppressed by Nectin-4–blocking antibodies. Notably, Nectin-4 is also a measles virus receptor, suggesting shared host factors across these distinct viruses. This discovery advances understanding of rubella airway shedding and maternal–fetal transmission and may inform antiviral or vaccine strategies against congenital rubella syndrome. Background: global congenital rubella cases around 30,000/year (2019).

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infection in a woman in the prefecture; possible contact with an unspecified number of people at a facility in Matsuyama City.
articles.summary: Measles infection has been confirmed in a woman in her 50s in Ehime Prefecture, with possible exposure to an unspecified number of people at two Matsuyama City facilities during the infectious period. As of Oct 23, this is the prefecture's third confirmed measles case this year. Two exposure sites: Sogo Mart Uemoto Store (Kita-Uemoto-cho) in Matsuyama City, on Oct 19 from 5:00–5:20 pm; and Supermarket Nitto Kume Store (Minami-Kume-cho) on Oct 21 from 9:05–9:15 am. The article notes airborne measles virus can survive less than two hours. The woman had visited the same location as a man in his 30s confirmed infected in Matsuyama City on Oct 10. Measles is highly contagious, and infection can occur in those without immunity after exposure. The health department is advising customers who may have visited the sites during those times to monitor for symptoms and seek guidance.

articles.headline: 50代女性がはしか感染 スーパー2店舗を利用したとして県が注意を呼びかけ 愛媛
articles.headlineTranslated: A woman in her 50s contracted measles; Ehime Prefecture warns after she used two supermarkets.
articles.summary: Measles confirmed in Ehime Prefecture: A woman in her 50s living in the Chūyō Health Center jurisdiction has tested positive, marking Ehime’s third measles case this year. Illness began with fever, sore throat and a rash around Oct 20; she sought care in Matsuyama on Oct 22, with genetic testing confirming measles on Oct 23. She had one prior measles vaccination and no overseas travel history. She visited two Matsuyama supermarkets on Oct 19 and Oct 21, prompting the prefecture to advise customers who shopped there on those dates to monitor for symptoms. Nationwide, measles cases reached 579 this year. The article does not specify an infection source and does not indicate importation/exportation details.
